quality_assessment: Chapter is comprehensive, well-structured, and highly accurate. It covers all major automatic filtering mechanisms with excellent examples and clear explanations. Only minor enhancements and cross-references would improve it further.

issues.description: Chapter mentions --no-require-git but doesn't explain --require-git (the opposite flag)
issues.current_content:
By default, `.gitignore` files are only respected inside Git repositories. Use `--no-require-git` to respect `.gitignore` files even outside repositories:

```bash
$ rg 'pattern' --no-require-git
```
issues.should_add: Also mention --require-git as the explicit way to enforce default behavior
issues.fix_suggestion: Add note: 'The default behavior can be made explicit with --require-git, which ensures .gitignore files are only respected inside git repositories.'

issues.description: Chapter lists 'symlinks' in topics but doesn't explicitly discuss symlink handling in automatic filtering context
issues.should_add: Brief explanation of how symlinks interact with automatic filtering (default: don't follow, -L/--follow flag)
issues.fix_suggestion:
Add subsection under 'Advanced Filtering' or in 'Common Use Cases' explaining:
- By default, ripgrep doesn't follow symlinks
- Use -L/--follow to follow symlinks
- Loop detection is automatic
- Interaction with ignore files when following symlinks

issues.current_content:
| Flag | Effect |
|------|--------|
| `--no-ignore` | Disable all standard ignore files |
| `--no-ignore-dot` | Disable `.ignore` and `.rgignore` files only |
| `--no-ignore-vcs` | Disable `.gitignore` and `.git/info/exclude` only |
| `--no-ignore-global` | Disable global gitignore only |
| `--no-ignore-parent` | Don't read ignore files from parent directories |
| `--no-ignore-files` | Disable custom ignore files from `--ignore-file` |
issues.fix_suggestion:
Add row to table:
| `--no-ignore-exclude` | Disable .git/info/exclude only |

issues.fix_suggestion: Add space or separate backticks: either `-. / --hidden` or `-.`/`--hidden` for better readability

issues.description: Chapter explains NUL byte heuristic but doesn't specify how many bytes are scanned
issues.current_content:
Ripgrep uses a NUL byte (`\0`) heuristic:
- If a file contains a NUL byte in the first few kilobytes, it's considered binary
issues.should_be: More specific about the threshold (though implementation details may vary)
issues.fix_suggestion: Consider adding more detail if implementation is stable, or keep vague to allow implementation flexibility. Current wording 'first few kilobytes' is acceptable but could reference --max-columns-preview if that affects binary detection.
issues.source_reference: tests/binary.rs comments mention 'first few KB' with mmap, crates/printer/src/summary.rs:684-745
